newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, Aug 29.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, Aug 29.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - Leading British shares broke back below the 3,900 level as U.S. economic data raised the spectre of higher interest rates and traders took the chance to mark prices lower. The FTSE 100 index had earlier climbed to 3,8921.1 just below it's record of 3,922.1, before edging down through the afternoon session to finish the day at 3,885.0, a fall of 33.7 points.

FRANKFURT - German equities ended bourse trade mixed after a strong earnings report from Daimler-Benz AG triggered profit-taking on the giant industrial group's stock instead of giving the market a much-needed lift. The 30-share DAX index, which tracks Germany's 30 blue chip shares, ended the bourse session down 3.10 points, or 0.12 percent, at 2,560.06. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 2,548.84.

PARIS - French stocks finished near their session lows, pressured by the franc's weakness, fears of possible industrial unrest and stronger-than-expected U.S. economic data. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 25.34 points or 1.27 percent to 1,977.56.

ZURICH - Swiss shares slid into negative terrain towards the end of the session to finish lower after the U.S. data awakened interest rate fears. Market attention focused on Roche, Ciba and Sandoz and on insurer Swiss Re. Pharmaceuticals were still battered as market disappointment with the companies' half-year figures persisted. The All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) lost 5.26 points or 0.22 percent to close at 2,361.03.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed lower, as concern about Japan's economic recovery lingered in the market following Wednesday's weak "tankan" data. Most buyers retreated to the sidelines, and the sluggish trade is expected to continue until September. The key 225-share Nikkei average shed 156.65 points or 0.76 percent to end at 20,553.16.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended weaker, with a share placement from New World Development dulling the market's tone. The Hang Seng index fell 51.28 points to close at 11,328.21.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market meandered to a weaker close, having spent the day trapped in a 10 point range with little incentive to attempt to escape. The All Ordinaries index lost 4.9 points to close at 2279.3.

JOHANNESBURG - After busy trade, South African all-share and industrial indices finished safely higher but off their day's best levels in a market underpinned by futures dealings. Futures arbitrage had dominated trade with players buying equities and selling into the futures market. The Overall index was up 25.1 points at 6,704.4, Industrials were up 15.9 points to 7,853.8 and Golds added 21.8 to 1,808.7.
